title: Vana: exile
hook: Vyasa walks into the forest camp with a plan: the waiting can become preparation, and Arjuna must go alone

segments.voice: Yesterday in the Vana, Bhima wanted to fight and Yudhishthira kept his word. Your line was Vana: exile. Did you keep one small word exactly as you gave it? Day seven hundred eighty-one.

The argument has gone as far as it can go. Bhima wants them stronger, and soon. Yudhishthira won't break his word, and he knows how formidable the warriors on the other side are. The brothers are stuck between impatience and patience. And into that stuck place walks an old sage. It's Vyasa, the grandfather of both the Pandavas and the Kauravas, and he has come with a way out. Today, the visitor who turns waiting into a plan.
screen: `STUCK BETWEEN IMPATIENCE AND PATIENCE.` → `VYASA WALKS IN.` → `WAITING BECOMES A PLAN.`

segments.voice: Vyasa takes Yudhishthira aside. I know what's in your heart, he says, the fear of Bhishma and Drona and Karna. So here's what to do. He gives Yudhishthira a sacred knowledge to teach to Arjuna, a kind of inner discipline that will let him reach the gods. And he says: Arjuna must go. He must seek out the gods themselves, Indra and Rudra and the guardians of the world, and win their weapons through ascetic effort. That is how the Pandavas will be ready when the time of exile ends. Now the argument looks different. Bhima wanted action, and here it is. Yudhishthira wanted to keep his word, and he does. Nobody breaks the terms; nobody leaves the forest early. But the waiting stops being empty. It becomes a time to grow. And then notice the cost. Arjuna has to go alone. The brothers who have shared everything, even exile, will be apart. Yudhishthira teaches him what Vyasa taught, and Arjuna prepares to leave, armed, toward the mountains of the north. In the epic, Draupadi speaks a blessing over him as he goes, wishing him success and asking that the gods protect him on the road. Vana, the forest, has carried the Pandavas through a lot: the sun's vessel, Krishna's visit, the long arguments. Now it becomes something else, a base camp. One brother walks out of it, and tomorrow we follow him up the mountain.
screen: `VYASA TAKES YUDHISHTHIRA ASIDE.` · `A KNOWLEDGE FOR ARJUNA.` · `SEEK THE WEAPONS OF THE GODS.` · then, large: `THE WAITING BECOMES GROWING.`

segments.voice: Settle in, and let the breath become slow and easy. Bring to mind some waiting in your own life: a season you can't hurry, an answer that hasn't come. Breathe in, and feel how it sits in you. Breathe out, and ask, gently, what this waiting could be for. Is there one small thing it could prepare you for? Don't force an answer; just let the question breathe with you. If you pray, you can bring that waiting into your prayer. If not, rest in the question. The bell holds the time.
Vana. The forest of exile, which becomes a base camp the day Vyasa sends Arjuna to seek the weapons of the gods.
Your line: Vana: exile. Today, take one stretch of waiting, a line, a commute, a slow afternoon, and use it to prepare for something. Day seven hundred eighty-one.

howItsDone: Retellings of the Mahabharata mark Vyasa's visit as the turn in the forest years, when Arjuna leaves to seek divine weapons; tradition names Vyasa as the epic's composer as well as a character in it.

original.note: Sanskrit Vyāsa: the sage who visits the camp, named by tradition as the composer of the Mahabharata.

trapdoor: what you thought: an old sage drops by to comfort them.
what it means: Vyasa gives a plan, a knowledge for Arjuna, who must seek the gods' weapons alone.
what a scholar hears: tradition names Vyasa as the epic's composer, so the author steps into his own story to move it forward.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Aranyaka Parva), Vyasa's visit to the Pandavas (the knowledge given to Yudhishthira for Arjuna; Arjuna sent to obtain weapons from the gods; Arjuna's departure and Draupadi's blessing)

notes: All paraphrase. Ganguli calls the knowledge 'Pratismriti'; the script describes it rather than naming it. Keeper may want the name.
